report.headline: Usage projected to fall from 24.7% in the EuroLeague to 19.8% in the NBA, landing near league average, while the shooting projection carries no reliable information

projection.text: Projected usage rate in the NBA is 19.8%, down from a EuroLeague usage rate of 24.7% (+1.04 sd above league average), landing just below the NBA average of 20.1%.

risks.text: The usage projection rests on only 61 historical EL->NBA transitions, and the fitted carry-over slope of 0.575 means just over half of his above-average standing is expected to transfer.
The true shooting projection (52.4%, 80% interval 46.8%-58.0%) should not be trusted: the model's out-of-fold error (4.5%) is worse than simply guessing the league mean (4.3%).
Even the usage projection carries an 80% interval spanning 15.1%-24.6%, roughly two league standard deviations (4.8%), limiting confidence in any single-season usage estimate.

strengths.text: Produced at a high assist rate (25.8%) and 4.693 assists per 75 possessions in the EuroLeague, alongside a moderate turnover rate of 17.3%.
Scored 16.571 points per 75 possessions on a EuroLeague true shooting percentage of 56.5%, roughly at the EuroLeague average (+0.06 sd).

His EuroLeague usage rate of 24.7% placed him +1.04 sd above the league average, well above the +0.46 sd average standing of players who historically made this move, indicating a genuinely high-usage profile even among selected movers.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate runs from 15.1% to 24.6% — nearly two standard deviations of the NBA usage distribution (SD 4.8%) — and the 95% interval widens further to 12.5%-27.1%, so the model can rank this player relative to peers but cannot pin down an individual point estimate; the true-shooting projection carries no information at all because it is outperformed by the league-mean baseline (4.5% MAE vs 4.3%).
